body.statement: For every fixed compact time interval, uniformly over \(p\in\mathcal P\) and \(\gamma\in[-G,G]\), the stationary paths \(X_{0,N}\) and \(X_{1,N}\) converge in bounded-Lipschitz distance on Skorokhod space to the stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process \(X_0\) and stationary piecewise Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process \(X_\gamma\). For every \(f\in C_c^3(\mathbb R)\) and every fixed \(R_{\mathrm{loc}}<\infty\), the corresponding scaled generators satisfy \(\sup_{x\in E_{0,N}\cap[-R_{\mathrm{loc}},R_{\mathrm{loc}}]}|(G_{0,N}-\mathcal L_0)f(x)|+\sup_{x\in E_{1,N}\cap[-R_{\mathrm{loc}},R_{\mathrm{loc}}]}|(G_{1,N}-\mathcal L_{\gamma_N})f(x)|\to0\). Their invariant laws converge compact-uniformly to \(\pi_0\) and \(\pi_\gamma\), the Poisson construction uniquely determines centered solutions with \(1/D\le h_\gamma'(x)\le1/d\), and \(V_{0,N}\to V_0\), \(V_{1,N}\to V_\gamma\) uniformly.
body.justification: This theorem relates the actual scaled finite generators and stationary paths to the two limiting diffusions and makes the long-run variance evaluable.
body.gap: Boutilier, Jonasson, Li, and Yoeli give a fluid limit but no critical stationary path or Poisson-energy limit; Braverman and Dai study a different many-server system and a static-law metric.
body.consumer: Trial planners can compute the capacity-dependent precision curve without simulating each large finite chain.
